key_insight: A machine-learning model can predict DFT-quality Hamiltonians and combine them with efficient Green's-function solvers to make quantum transport simulations scale linearly with device length.
engineering_relevance: This enables predictive nanoelectronic device modeling at realistic sizes, including systems with over 10,000 atoms, at costs far below fully self-consistent DFT-NEGF.
method: Train an E(3)-equivariant GNN on conventional DFT Hamiltonians from small structures.
Use the predicted Hamiltonians with DFT-derived electrode self-energies, recursive Green's functions, and a nonorthogonal kernel polynomial method.
Avoid transport self-consistency, enabling faster runs and compatibility with hybrid functionals like HSE06.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks on Pt-Si-Pt, doped Pt-Si:P-Pt, and Pt-molecule-Pt junctions show meV-level Hamiltonian accuracy, faithful transmission spectra, and more than three orders of magnitude speedup for sub-500-atom devices.
watch_item: The zero-bias Hamiltonian approximation is best suited to weakly nonlinear regimes, so accuracy may degrade under stronger finite-bias transport conditions.
paper_title: Linear-Scaling Quantum Transport from Machine-Learning Density Functional Theory Hamiltonians
